proposals.sourceEvidence: bhrāturjāyā f. 'brother's wife' lex., [bhrātr̥jāyā- f. Kālid. — bhrā́tr̥-, jāyā́-] Pk. bhāujāyā-, bhāujjā-, °jāiā- f., Dm. brāžäi, Paš.lauṛ. lāǰā́, Gaw. blāzṓe, Kho. bražayu; Bshk. ǰāǰā 'brother's wife, father's brother's son's wife'; Tor. bežḗ 'brother's wife', Phal. brahàžäi, brāǰäi; Sh. jăẓḗ f. '(woman's) brother's wife, husband's sister' (→ Ḍ. jajε); S. bhāj̄āī f. 'brother's wife', L. P. bharjāī f.; Ku. bhauj, °jī 'elder brother's wife', N. bhāuju, °jyu (< bhāuj jyu); OB. bhāuja, B. bhāuj, bhāji, bhāj, Or. bhāuja; Mth. bhaujāi, bhāũji 'elder brother's wife'; Bhoj. Aw.lakh. bhaujāī 'brother's wife', H. bhaujāī, bhaujī, bhāuj f., OMarw. bhāvaja f., G. bhɔjāī f., M. bhāvj̈aī f., Ko. bhāvaja. — Pk. bhāujjā- &c. shortened from *bhāujjāyā- rather than bhrātr̥bhāryā- f. Gaut. Addenda: bhrāturjāyā-: S.kcch. bhojāī f. 'brother's wife', WPah.poet. bhrauj̈ f. (obl. -i) 'brother's (esp. elder brother's) wife'.
